title: Attorney General of Colorado

context.text: Colorado's Secretary of State certified the 2026 general-election ballot on September 4, 2026; the state's official general-election candidate list shows Michael J. Allen (Republican) and Jena Griswold (Democratic) for Attorney General.

Incumbent Attorney General Phil Weiser is term-limited. Griswold won the June 30 Democratic primary with 44.2% over David Seligman, Michael Dougherty and Hetal Doshi; Allen won the Republican primary with 59.9% over David Willson.

summary.text: Jena Griswold is the Democratic nominee. She is the term-limited Colorado Secretary of State, an office she has held since 2019, and a former voting-rights attorney. Her campaign says her priorities are fighting federal actions affecting Colorado, holding federal immigration agents accountable, taking on large corporations and defending reproductive freedom.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in politics and Spanish literature from Whitman College and a law degree from the University of Pennsylvania.
Worked as an attorney focused on voter protection and international anti-corruption cases, and served as director of Gov. John Hickenlooper's Washington, D.C. office.
Has served as Colorado Secretary of State since 2019.

priorities.text: Fighting Trump administration actions that affect Colorado.
Holding ICE and other federal agents accountable.

positions.summary: In her candidate questionnaire answers she says she will work to ensure access to reproductive care including abortion access.
positions.quote: I will do everything I can to make sure that all Coloradans have access to reproductive care, including birth control, IVF, and abortion access.

positions.summary: In her candidate questionnaire answers she says she will fight to pass a stronger ban on assault weapons.
positions.quote: As Attorney General, I will fight to pass a stronger ban on assault weapons.

record.text: As Secretary of State, announced on September 14, 2026 that her office had marked 12,693 business-registry entities as fraudulent and removed 10,214 more in the first month under House Bill 26-1088, a law she said she championed.
Announced on August 26, 2026 that Colorado joined 23 other states and the District of Columbia in suing the U.S. Postal Service over rules limiting who can receive a mail ballot.
Certified the 2026 Colorado general-election ballot on September 4, 2026.

candidates.name: Michael Allen
candidates.currentRole: District Attorney, Colorado's 4th Judicial District (El Paso and Teller counties; since 2021)

summary.text: Michael Allen is the Republican nominee. A U.S. Navy veteran and career prosecutor, he is the elected District Attorney for the 4th Judicial District, first elected in 2020 and re-elected in 2024. His campaign centers on public safety, taxpayer spending, fighting corruption and consumer protection.

background.text: Enlisted in the U.S. Navy after high school; earned an undergraduate degree from the University of Northern Colorado and a law degree from the University of Kansas.
Has worked in prosecution for more than 20 years, beginning as a law-school intern in 2004, including as a consumer-protection prosecutor in the Kansas Attorney General's Office.
Elected District Attorney in the 4th Judicial District in 2020 and re-elected in 2024; his campaign says he created an Organized Crime Unit and a motor vehicle theft team.

priorities.text: Public safety: supporting law enforcement, protecting victims and targeting criminal organizations that operate across county lines.
Reviewing the Attorney General's Office budget to eliminate waste; his campaign says the office budget has grown about 84% over seven years.
Investigating government corruption and fraud, and pursuing consumer-protection cases including scams and deceptive practices.
Defending Colorado's water rights and insisting other states honor compact obligations.

record.text: Serves as elected District Attorney of Colorado's 4th Judicial District; his campaign says his office prosecuted the Club Q shooting case as a hate crime.

researchNotes: Slate confirmed against the Colorado Secretary of State's official 2026 General Election candidate list; no other parties' AG candidates appear on it. Griswold's positions come from her own candidate questionnaire answers as published by KRDO; a climate position that appeared only in Ballotpedia's quotation of her campaign website was removed because the original could not be found. Allen's campaign-site claims about his office are his own statements. Allen's positions on the guide's fixed issues were not found as direct statements.
